text.p: Italian bonds and futures started firmer with good buying interest seen as the Bank of Spain cut its key money interest rate, while firmer overnight T-bonds and a higher lira also gave support, dealers said.

They added that the Spanish rate cut focused investors minds on Italian May preliminary CPI data due next week which is likely to see a further fall in inflation and could prompt the Bank of Italy into an interest rate cut.
"The Bank of Spain's cut has made people think about a possible Bank of Italy rate cut next week," said one trader on the LIFFE market.
The Bank of Spain cut its key money rate to 5.25 percent from 5.50 percent at today's regular repurchase tender for central bank certificates.

In Italy, preliminary CPI inflation data is due next week and analysts forecast May inflation will slow to 1.5 percent year on year from 1.7 percent in April, and this may prompt the Italian central bank into cutting its discount rate.
"Much of the rally in prices this week has come from talk of a rate cut in Italy so the move in Spain together with the strength in the lira has encouraged these hopes," said the LIFFE trader.
By 0755 GMT, the LIFFE June futures contract was 41 basis points higher at 130.62.
